version.changelog:
Agent Times 3.0.0 — Adds sentiment analysis and webhook notifications.

- Search results now include sentiment labels (bullish, bearish, neutral) and sentiment scores (-1 to 1) on `/ask`.
- New free /subscribe webhook endpoint for real-time topic monitoring; agents can receive new article notifications matching their queries.
- Unsubscribe endpoint (`DELETE /subscribe/:id`) added for webhook management.
- Documentation updated to reflect these new endpoints and fields.
- Other endpoints and API usage unchanged.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it documents a public news/search HTTP API and only requires curl; there are no unexplained credentials, installs, or asks to access local files.

dimensions.detail: Name/description describe a news/search API and SKILL.md contains detailed curl examples for those same endpoints. The only declared runtime dependency is curl, which matches the documented usage.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions tell the agent to call public HTTP endpoints (GET /ask, /trending, etc.) and to POST a webhook URL to /subscribe. This is within scope, but the subscription feature will cause the service to POST to any webhook URL you provide — avoid registering internal or sensitive endpoints (localhost, internal IPs, cloud metadata endpoints) to prevent unintended network deliveries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files; nothing is written to disk or downloaded by the skill itself, which is the lowest-risk pattern.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to simply document how to call the Agent Times public API using curl. Before installing or using it: 1) Treat webhooks carefully — do not provide internal, localhost, or metadata endpoints as your webhook URL (the service will POST to whatever URL you register). 2) Confirm how paid endpoints and Base/x402 micropayments are handled (they may require an external wallet or portal). 3) Validate incoming webhook requests on your endpoint (signatures, TLS) before processing. 4) Review the service's privacy/retention policy if you will send or receive sensitive data via subscriptions. 5) Because this is instruction-only and uses curl, the attack surface is limited, but only use the skill with trusted endpoints and follow the webhook precautions above.
